subject: Order of model comparisons in lavTestLRT for measurement invariance

messages.author: ac589741b29f67f1
messages.subject: Order of model comparisons in lavTestLRT for measurement invariance
parts:
The documentation for lavTestLRT reads that it returns: "...When given a sequence of objects, this function tests the models against one another in the order specified." I am wondering if that is consistently true, particularly in the case of measurement invariance testing?

My context: I've scripted four dyadic invariance models (configural, loading, intercept, residual), however, rather than what we might call a "tear down" approach (where we start with the most unparsimonious model as baseline, and incrementally "tear it down" to whatever level of parsimony [invariance] is supported), I'd like to pursue a "build up" approach (starting with the most parsimonious model as baseline, and incrementally "building it up" to whatever level of complexity [noninvariance] is necessary). I don't think my models or reasons for desiring this approach are particularly important to answering the question here, but I can provide them if folks think they are germane.

The problem: when I actually run the nested model comparisons, lavTestLRT/anova are indifferent to the order that I specify. That is the following four lines all generate the same order of output:

anova(sat.config.fit, sat.loading.fit, sat.intercept.fit, sat.residual.fit)
anova(sat.residual.fit, sat.intercept.fit, sat.loading.fit, sat.config.fit)

lavTestLRT(sat.config.fit, sat.loading.fit, sat.intercept.fit, sat.residual.fit)
lavTestLRT(sat.residual.fit, sat.intercept.fit, sat.loading.fit, sat.config.fit)

The output consistently has the configural model as the topmost/first model in the output, followed by the loading, followed by the intercept, followed by the residual (I suspect it's just ordering from least : greatest df). 

At the risk of embarrassing myself (as I find myself questioning things I took for granted), is the "build up" approach in this case not valid with the LRT approach? (i.e., is there some reason testing *decreases* in X^2 is logically incoherent/bad form?) 

And if not, is there some secret sauce to getting lavTestLRT to compare the models in the sequence I desire. I am not opposed to writing my own boutique function to serve this purpose (if it's a reasonable testing approach), but it would be preferable if I didn't have to.

messages.subject: AW: Order of model comparisons in lavTestLRT for measurement invariance
parts:
Maybe I don't understand your question correctly, sorry. If I understand the problem correctly, you just have to read the results from bottom to top or sort the data.frame accordingly. Something like this:

library(lavaan)

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit.config     <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, group = "school")
fit.loadings   <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, group = "school", group.equal = c("loadings"))
fit.intercepts <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, group = "school", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))
fit.residuals  <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, group = "school", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals"))

res <- lavTestLRT(fit.config, fit.loadings, fit.intercepts, fit.residuals)

res[order(-res$Df),]

parts:
Thanks Christian, 

I guess to be more clear, I am asking two questions, each of a different sort:

1. A more technical package functionality-oriented question: The language in the documentation for lavTestLRT states: "When given a sequence of objects, this function tests the models against one another in the order specified."  I am asking, therefore, whether the documentation is in err (or if it's not in err, if this is a minor bug for lavTestLRT, if it ought to be providing the reverse-ordered output given my reverse-order of specified models)? And:
2. A more substantive application question: I am asking whether this "build-up" approach is statistically/logically valid? I was pretty confident it was, but that lavTestLRT insisted on the "tear down" arrangement of output regardless of model order specified  had me second guessing myself. 

Your solution for reordering the output is effective and efficient but I wasn't so much worried about whether I could reorder the output, inasmuch as I was wondering whether, given the documentation, lavTestLRT ought to already be doing this given my specified order (question 1), and whether even if I could reorganize the table in code, whether this altered order was a valid testing procedure (question 2).

HTH

Hi John, 

no, I do not have a GH account. You don't have to mention me there. That's perfectly fine. 

A note on lavTestLRT: apparently lavTestLRT only compares the model with the model that has the closest df distance. It would be great if there was an option to compare a model to all nested models. Amos does that (or did, I don't use Amos anymore). A (pointless) example: lavTestLRT compares the configural model to the model with constrained regressions model, but not to the model with constrained regressions and intercepts, even though the latter model is also nested within the configural model. Okay, the example makes little sense, but there are perfectly reasonable applications from my point of view. Maybe you can mention that as well?

Best

Christian

The documentation for lavTestLRT reads that it returns: "...When given a sequence of objects, this function tests the models against one another in the order specified." I am wondering if that is consistently true, particularly in the case of measurement invariance testing?

My context: I've scripted four dyadic invariance models (configural, loading, intercept, residual), however, rather than what we might call a "tear down" approach (where we start with the most unparsimonious model as baseline, and incrementally "tear it down" to whatever level of parsimony [invariance] is supported), I'd like to pursue a "build up" approach (starting with the most parsimonious model as baseline, and incrementally "building it up" to whatever level of complexity [noninvariance] is necessary). I don't think my models or reasons for desiring this approach are particularly important to answering the question here, but I can provide them if folks think they are germane.

The problem: when I actually run the nested model comparisons, lavTestLRT/anova are indifferent to the order that I specify. That is the following four lines all generate the same order of output:

anova(sat.config.fit, sat.loading.fit, sat.intercept.fit, sat.residual.fit)
anova(sat.residual.fit, sat.intercept.fit, sat.loading.fit, sat.config.fit)

lavTestLRT(sat.config.fit, sat.loading.fit, sat.intercept.fit, sat.residual.fit)
lavTestLRT(sat.residual.fit, sat.intercept.fit, sat.loading.fit, sat.config.fit)

The output consistently has the configural model as the topmost/first model in the output, followed by the loading, followed by the intercept, followed by the residual (I suspect it's just ordering from least : greatest df). 

At the risk of embarrassing myself (as I find myself questioning things I took for granted), is the "build up" approach in this case not valid with the LRT approach? (i.e., is there some reason testing *decreases* in X^2 is logically incoherent/bad form?) 

And if not, is there some secret sauce to getting lavTestLRT to compare the models in the sequence I desire. I am not opposed to writing my own boutique function to serve this purpose (if it's a reasonable testing approach), but it would be preferable if I didn't have to.

--

messages.subject: Re: Order of model comparisons in lavTestLRT for measurement invariance
parts: John,

You wrote:
>>>
2. A more substantive application question: I am asking whether this "build-up" approach is statistically/logically valid? I was pretty confident it was, but that lavTestLRT insisted on the "tear down" arrangement of output regardless of model order specified  had me second guessing myself.
>>>

I may be misunderstanding your question but Peter Bentler (2000), in the section on nested tests, stated that when you begin with the most general model and test the result of adding a constraint, the sequential tests are statistically independent of one another.  However, if you begin with the most restricted model and release constraints, this independence between successive tests does not hold.

Keith

Peter M. Bentler (2000) Rites, Wrongs, and Gold in Model Testing, Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 7:1, 82-91, DOI: 10.1207/S15328007SEM0701_04

My thanks as well, Keith. 

In reading the Bentler piece, I am curious as to how he came to believe the independence did not hold with the "build up" testing sequence (i.e., starting with most restrictive). I've gone through Steiger et al. (1985) a few times now, and best I can tell (admittedly quite fallible because navigating proofs is decidedly not a long-suit of mine), I'm not under the impression that Steiger et al. indulged the "build up" order, but rather, it seems they exclusively focused on the "tear down" (i.e., starting with the least restrictive). At the very least, their Monte Carlo simulations seem exclusively focused on the latter. Of course, maybe Bentler did the simulations with the "build up" approach himself and found the independence established in Steiger et al did not hold (and that's what motivated the remark), but I'm left wondering where to find some more detail about the extent of the problem. 

Still, really appreciate the very promising lead!

-John
